text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore workers should be allowed to draw up individual contracts with their employers that will supercede the collective agreements secured by their unions, Lim Boon Heng, secretary-general of the National Trade Union Congress, told a May Day rally.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin has stressed that Chinese officials will be working closely with Singaporean counterparts on the Suzhou industrial park project.
- U.S. PresidentBill Clinton has said he is "quite satisfied" with China's assurances that Hong Kong will enjoy high degree of autonomy after the July 1 handover of sovereignty.

- A victory for Tony Blair's New Labour Party seemed inevitable. Four up-to-the-minute polls of voting intentions published, agree that his overall majority will be from 100 to 180 seats in Britain's 659-member parliament.
- More publicly-listed companies have opted to issue shareholders with abridged versions of their annual reports, saving several hundred thousand sollars a year.
- Singapore's Keppel Corporation signed a one billion peso ($57.8 million) rescue package for an ailing Philipiine thrift bank, Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank.
- Dozens of Singapore and foreign firms are circling the depressed Thai property market for good bargains.

- U.S. dollar roared to a near five-year high of 127.45 yen in Tokyo as technical obstacles restraining the U.S. currency's rise were eliminated and fears of possible Japan and G-7 intervention appeared to fade.

- A hotly-contested battle for customers is developing among Petrol stations in Singapore n the arena of service and convenience stores with firms pumping millions of dollars are in to provide such services.
